written: 2026-10-01, before any SMILES were fetched or any model fitted
question: Can a selectivity QSAR trained DIRECTLY on ddG beat the difference-of-two-predictions approaches (co-folding, MM-GBSA, free energy) for YGGFEVVG?
target: ddG = RT*ln(Ki_mu / Ki_delta); POSITIVE = delta-preferring (repo convention)
training_set: ChEMBL compounds with Ki at BOTH OPRD1 (CHEMBL236) and OPRM1 (CHEMBL233); primary tier requires >=2 measurements per receptor (n=227), secondary tier >=1 (n=3584). Single-source by rule: ChEMBL only.
features: Morgan fingerprint r=2, 2048 bits + MW, cLogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds
model: gradient-boosted trees, default hyperparameters, no tuning on the test folds
validation: Bemis-Murcko scaffold-grouped 5-fold CV. Scaffold split is the honest one and is what the gates are judged on; random split reported for contrast only.

gates.G1_correlation: AMENDED before any data was fetched: the p=0.05 critical r is 0.13 at n=227 and 0.033 at n=3584, so a significance-based gate passes automatically and tests nothing. Replaced with a USEFULNESS threshold: |Pearson r| >= 0.50 on pooled scaffold-split held-out predictions.
gates.G2_sign: sign accuracy on held-out predictions must exceed 50% by a binomial test at p<0.05
gates.G3_applicability: max Tanimoto similarity of YGGFEVVG to any training compound must be >= 0.30
gates.G1b_resolution: RMSE on scaffold-split held-out predictions must be <= 1.0 kcal/mol. Rationale: the effect to resolve is ~1 kcal/mol (met-enkephalin +0.81, our calibrated engPENK estimate +1.23). A model with RMSE above that cannot distinguish our peptide from no preference, however well it correlates across a 10 kcal/mol range.

decision_rule: If G1 OR G2 fails -> NO prediction for YGGFEVVG is reported, consistent with Cycle 7. If G3 fails -> any prediction is reported as OUT OF DOMAIN and is not usable evidence, even if G1 and G2 pass.
stated_prior: Likely to fail G3. The training set is dominated by small molecules; YGGFEVVG is an 8-residue peptide. This is the same applicability-domain problem the earlier fingerprint screen hit. Predicting failure in advance so a pass is informative.
what_would_make_this_better_than_prior_m: Selectivity is the direct regression target, so it does not pay the sqrt(2) error inflation that every difference-of-two-predictions method pays.
amendment_note: G1 was amended and G1b added at pre-registration time, before fetching SMILES or fitting. The original significance-based G1 is recorded above so the change is visible.
